01_basic_object._description: A JSON object stores data using key-value pairs enclosed in curly braces {}.
01_basic_object.name: SmartQuiz

02_multiple_properties._description: An object can hold multiple properties separated by commas.

03_strings._description: Text data must be enclosed in double quotes.

04_numbers._description: JSON supports integers and decimal numbers. Quotes are not used for numbers.

05_booleans._description: Booleans represent true or false. They must be lowercase and without quotes.

06_null._description: null represents the intentional absence of a value. It must be lowercase and without quotes.

07_arrays._description: An array is an ordered list of items enclosed in square brackets [].

08_array_of_strings._description: A list containing only text strings.

10_array_of_objects._description: A list where each item is an object. Very common in API responses.

11_nested_objects._description: An object placed inside another object. This creates a hierarchy.

12_objects_inside_arrays._description: Similar to array of objects, but emphasizing the nesting level.

13_arrays_inside_objects._description: A property whose value is an array.

14_empty_object._description: An object with no properties. Useful as a default placeholder.

15_empty_array._description: An array with no items. Useful for initializing a list before adding data.

16_double_quotes_and_keys._description: In JSON, keys MUST be strings enclosed in double quotes. Single quotes are invalid.

17_invalid_json_examples._description: Standard JSON does not allow single quotes, unquoted keys, trailing commas, or comments. Here are invalid examples represented as strings to keep this file valid.

18_corrected_json_examples._description: The corrected versions of the invalid examples above.

19_escape_sequences._description: Special characters inside strings must be escaped using a backslash \.

20_unicode_characters._description: You can include special unicode characters (like emojis) using \u followed by the hex code.

21_long_strings._description: Long text must be kept on a single physical line. Use \n for line breaks instead of pressing Enter.
21_long_strings.description: This is a very long string that represents a paragraph. Even if it gets very long, it must stay on one line in the JSON file. To break lines, use \n like this: Line 1.\nLine 2.

22_nested_json._description: Combining objects, arrays, and nested objects to represent complex real-world data.

23_real_world_user_data._description: A typical user object returned from a database or API.

24_real_world_product_data._description: A typical product object for an e-commerce application.

25_real_world_student_data._description: A student object containing nested arrays and objects.

26_real_world_quiz_data._description: A quiz object with questions and options, typical for an app like SmartQuiz.

27_api_request_body._description: Data sent from frontend to backend (e.g., a POST request to create a user).

28_api_success_response._description: Standard structure for a successful API response.

29_api_error_response._description: Standard structure for an API error response.

30_rest_api_response_structure._description: A complex API response including pagination metadata and an array of data items.

31_json_parse_example._description: JSON cannot contain JavaScript code. This shows how JSON.parse() is used, represented as a string.
31_json_parse_example.concept: JSON.parse() converts a JSON string into a JavaScript object.

32_json_stringify_example._description: This shows how JSON.stringify() is used, represented as a string.
32_json_stringify_example.concept: JSON.stringify() converts a JavaScript object into a JSON string.

33_json_vs_javascript_object._description: JSON is a string format. JavaScript objects are memory structures. JSON requires double quotes for all keys and string values.

34_json_vs_yaml._description: YAML relies on indentation and dashes. JSON relies on curly braces and square brackets. YAML supports comments, JSON does not.

35_json_limitations._description: JSON cannot represent Dates, undefined, Functions, NaN, or Infinity directly. They must be converted to strings or null.
35_json_limitations.undefinedHandling: If a JS property is undefined, JSON.stringify() removes the key entirely.
35_json_limitations.nanHandling: If a JS property is NaN, JSON.stringify() converts it to null.

36_complex_real_world_example._description: A complete configuration example combining all concepts: objects, arrays, nested data, and various data types.

37_json_structure_summary._description: A quick reference summary of JSON data types.
syntaxRules: Keys must be strings in double quotes
